propositions: The first MCP initialize request after redeploy exceeds 30-second timeout while subsequent requests complete instantly because the first client lands behind a long synchronous tool call that blocks the event loop.

Every rebar MCP tool is defined as synchronous and the SDK calls tool bodies directly inside the ASGI request coroutine, preventing any other request (initialize, tools/list, or health) from being served until the tool returns.
A single long-running tool call (such as review_plan at 15-20 minutes or list_tickets at 177 seconds) occupies one core at 100% CPU and starves all concurrent HTTP requests while the loop is blocked.

Synchronous tool bodies must run on a worker thread via anyio.to_thread.run_sync instead of on the event-loop thread to allow concurrent request handling and preserve context variables for op-cert signing.
Already-async tools must not be double-wrapped, and certified tools must retain their in-flight gauge instrumentation after the offload is applied for proper SIGTERM drain observation.
